conventions.convention: DMC is fixed in two equivalent ZF forms: the tree form says every pruned tree of height ω on every set A whose levels are nonempty has a subtree with nonempty finite levels (Fremlin's DMC per the item, attributed to Blass 1979), and the successor-menu form says every serial relation on every nonempty set admits a successor menu sequence; the exclusion A ≠ ∅ applies only to the menu form.

Singular values of a compact operator: the sequence (s_n(T))_{n≥1} is zero-padded with s_1(T) = ‖T‖ and the multiset of positive singular values is listed in decreasing order with positive labels; the singular systems (e_j)_{j∈J}, (f_j)_{j∈J} are indexed by exactly the index set J of the positive singular values counted with multiplicity (J = {1,…,r} in finite rank r, J = {1,2,3,…} in infinite rank), and the padding zeros beyond the rank index no vectors.

Trace class is defined by finiteness of Σ_{n≥1} s_n(T) for the zero-padded singular-value sequence, with trace norm ‖T‖_1 := Σ_{m∈N} s_{m+1}(T) ∈ [0,+∞) and 0 ≤ s_n(T) ≤ s_1(T) = ‖T‖; the set is written S_1(H,K). The definition, and every trace-class item on the page, assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice AC_ω as its only choice principle.

A Hilbert basis E of H is supplied as data (its existence is never asserted), and the trace relative to E is tr_E(T) := Σ_{e∈E}⟨Te,e⟩ in the finite-subset-net sense of square-summable families; basis independence and equality with the basis-free trace are the content of a theorem, not of the definition.

Moore space means a regular T_1 space that is developable; a development is a sequence (G_n)_{n∈N} of open covers such that {St(x,G_n) : n ∈ N} is a neighbourhood base at every x, and every development may be replaced by the equivalent decreasing development G'_n of intersections G_0 ∩ … ∩ G_n.

PMEA asserts that for every cardinal λ the fair-coin product measure μ_λ on the finite-cylinder σ-algebra C_λ of 2^λ has a 𝔠-additive full extension to a probability measure on the full power set, where 𝔠 = 2^ℵ₀ and 𝔠-additive means additivity for disjoint families of size < 𝔠; PMEA-σ is the same with countably additive in place of 𝔠-additive. PMEA implies PMEA-σ, and neither axiom asks for a two-valued measure on λ.

Forcing order: q ≤ p means q is stronger than p. A Shelah sweetness model is a triple (P,D,(E_n)_{n<ω}) with 1_P a weakest condition, D ⊆ P dense (1_P need not lie in D), each E_n an equivalence relation on D with countably many classes and E_{n+1} refining E_n, every E_n-class downward directed, plus the sequential clause and the transfer clause (equivalently the comparable form used to synchronize a condition with a comparable one).

The Shelah inner model is N = HOD(S), computed in the generic extension V[G] of the CH-length sweet construction started over L, where S = ⋃_{α∈Ord} {}^{ω}α is the class of all countable sequences of ordinals; the real-and-ordinal presentation is asserted only in the branch over L, and no equality with L(ℝ), HOD(ℝ) or any class built from all ω₁-sequences of ordinals is claimed, nor is any ordinal collapsed.

On this page the scalar field is ℝ: X, Y, Z are real Banach spaces, U ⊆ X is open in the norm metric topology, and f is Fréchet differentiable at x when some T ∈ B(X,Y) satisfies lim_{h→0, h≠0} ‖f(x+h) − f(x) − Th‖/‖h‖ = 0; that T is written Df(x) and its operator norm is used throughout. No complex-valued derivative is introduced on this page.

A split C^k submanifold S of a Banach manifold M modelled on E is defined chartwise: at each p ∈ S there is a chart (φ,U) and a decomposition E = E_0 ⊕ E_1 into closed subspaces with bounded coordinate projections such that φ[U ∩ S] = φ[U] ∩ (E_0 ⊕ {0}); components may have non-isomorphic model spaces, so no single global model space is asserted.

A map f between C^1 Banach manifolds is Fredholm at p when Df(p) is a Fredholm operator (finite-dimensional kernel, closed range, finite-dimensional cokernel), is a Fredholm map when this holds at every point, and its index at p is dim ker Df(p) − dim coker Df(p); the phrase has index n is a separate global condition, and local constancy of p ↦ ind Df(p) is a theorem below, not part of the definition.

load_bearing.statement: Work in ZF. A node over A is a function t : n → A with n ∈ N; a tree of height ω on A is a set of nodes closed under initial segments and containing the empty node; DMC in tree form is the assertion that every pruned tree of height ω on every set A whose levels are nonempty has a subtree with nonempty finite levels, and DMC in successor-menu form is the assertion that every serial relation on every nonempty set admits a successor menu sequence.

Assume AC_ω. Let H be a real or complex Hilbert space and T ∈ B(H) compact self-adjoint, with Σ the set of nonzero eigenvalues and E_λ = ker(T − λI). Then Σ is a finite or countably infinite set of real numbers, each E_λ is finite dimensional, every point of the scalar field away from 0 has a neighbourhood meeting Σ finitely, so the only possible accumulation point is 0; the closed linear span M of ⋃_{λ∈Σ}E_λ satisfies M = (ker T)^⊥ = closure of ran T and H = M ⊕ M^⊥ with M^⊥ ⊆ ker T; for every x the finite-subset net Σ_{λ∈Σ} λP_λx converges in norm to Tx; and for complex H, σ(T) ∩ {μ ≠ 0} = Σ. No Hilbert basis of ker T is selected.

Assume AC_ω. Let T ∈ B(H,K) be compact, J the positive singular values counted with multiplicity (J = {1,…,r} when ran T is finite dimensional of dimension r, interpreted as ∅ when r = 0, and J = {1,2,3,…} when ran T is infinite dimensional). Then there are orthonormal families (e_j)_{j∈J} in (ker T)^⊥ and (f_j)_{j∈J} in closure of ran T with |T|e_j = s_je_j and f_j = s_j^{-1}Te_j; Tx = Σ_{j∈J} s_j⟨x,e_j⟩f_j in norm with ‖T − T_n‖ ≤ s_{n+1}; the map U sending e_j to f_j, extended by continuity to (ker T)^⊥ and by zero on ker T, is a partial isometry with T = U|T|, U*U the orthogonal projection onto (ker T)^⊥ and UU* the orthogonal projection onto closure of ran T; and the zero-padded sequence s_n(T) is not used to index the orthonormal systems, the zeros beyond the rank being numerical padding only.

Assume AC_ω; the bases E (of H), G (of K) and E_0 (of the auxiliary H_0) are supplied data and no Hilbert basis is asserted to exist. (1) If T ∈ B(H,K) is trace class, then with |T|, U and the singular system of T the operators B := |T|^{1/2} ∈ B(H) and A := U|T|^{1/2} ∈ B(H,K) satisfy T = AB, are both Hilbert–Schmidt relative to E, and ‖A‖_{HS,E} = ‖B‖_{HS,E} = ‖T‖_1^{1/2}. (2) Conversely, if T = AB with B ∈ B(H,H_0) Hilbert–Schmidt relative to E and A ∈ B(H_0,K) Hilbert–Schmidt relative to E_0, then T is trace class and ‖T‖_1 ≤ ‖A‖_{HS,E_0}‖B‖_{HS,E}.

Assume AC_ω and let T ∈ B(H) be trace class. Then (1) for every nuclear representation Tx = Σ_j⟨x,u_j⟩v_j (operator-norm convergence of partial sums, Σ_j‖u_j‖‖v_j‖ < +∞) the scalar series Σ_j⟨v_j,u_j⟩ converges absolutely with |Σ_j⟨v_j,u_j⟩| ≤ Σ_j‖u_j‖‖v_j‖; (2) this sum depends only on T and defines tr(T), without assuming that H has a Hilbert basis; (3) tr_E(T) = tr(T) for every supplied Hilbert basis E of H; (4) the trace is linear in the trace-class variable and |tr(T)| ≤ ‖T‖_1.
Over ZF, every compact Hausdorff space is a Baire space if and only if DMC holds.

ZF + DMC proves Urysohn's lemma: in a normal space any two disjoint closed sets F, G admit a continuous f : X → [0,1] with F ⊆ f^{-1}({0}) and G ⊆ f^{-1}({1}). DMC is used once, in its successor-menu form, to supply the finite menus of dyadic nodes.
Over ZF, the Axiom of Choice is equivalent to the assertion that every product of compact T1 spaces is compact.
Over ZF, BPI is equivalent to the compactness in the product topology of every product of spaces each carrying the cofinite topology.
In ZFC, every collectionwise normal Moore space is metrizable.
ZFC + PMEA proves the normal Moore space conjecture: every normal Moore space is metrizable. Already PMEA-σ suffices.

N satisfies: every subset of the reals has the property of Baire. Here the set-theoretic reals are represented first by Cantor space 2^ω, and the same assertion for the real line follows through comeagre homeomorphic coding subspaces; explicitly, for each real set A ∈ N there are in N an open set U and a meagre set M with A △ U ⊆ M.

The following theories are equiconsistent: ZFC; ZFC plus every real set first-order definable from a real and an ordinal parameter has the Baire property; and ZF+DC plus every set of reals has the Baire property. In particular Con(ZFC) is equivalent to Con(ZF+DC+ all real sets have BP), with no inaccessible-cardinal hypothesis.

ZFC plus an inaccessible cardinal and ZF+DC plus every set of reals Lebesgue measurable are equiconsistent. The same lower bound already follows from universal boldface Σ^1_3 measurability under Countable Choice.

Assume AC. Let X, Y be real Banach spaces, U ⊆ X open, f : U → Y of class C^k with k ≥ 1, and a ∈ U. If Df(a) : X → Y is a bounded linear isomorphism, then there are open U_0 ⊆ U with a ∈ U_0 and V_0 ⊆ Y with f(a) ∈ V_0 such that f|_{U_0} : U_0 → V_0 is a bijection whose inverse g := (f|_{U_0})^{-1} : V_0 → U_0 is of class C^k with Dg(f(x)) = Df(x)^{-1} for every x ∈ U_0.

concerns.concern: Indexing tension in the statement. It puts a_0(T) := ‖T‖ and for n ≥ 1 puts a_n(T) := inf{‖T − F‖ : dim ran F < n}, then says (a_n(T))_{n∈N} is a sequence in the library's zero-based convention and that, for compact T, a_n(T) = s_n(T) for every n, where (s_n(T)) is the zero-padded singular-value sequence indexed from n ≥ 1. With these definitions a_1(T) = s_1(T) = ‖T‖ = a_0(T) as well, and s_0 is never defined, so the equality can only mean n ≥ 1 (the trailing clause says so); as written, the phrase for every n invites the reading a_0(T) = s_0(T). The claim is true for n ≥ 1; only the indexing should be stated explicitly.

The statement introduces the sequence as λ_1 ≥ λ_2 ≥ ⋯ > 0, the positive eigenvalues of T listed with multiplicity, asserts s_n(T) = λ_n for every n and tr(T) = Σ_{n≥1} λ_n, and only afterwards says the equalities are also valid in the finite-rank case with λ_n := 0 for n beyond the rank. Taken literally the chain ⋯ > 0 defines a sequence that never contains 0 (and is empty for T = 0), so λ_n is undefined for n beyond the rank and s_n(T) = λ_n has no content there; the intended zero-padded reading of λ_n is supplied only by the later parenthetical.

seams_checked.note: The citing items use only the propositions those items state. def-fredholm-map-between-banach-manifolds restates finite-dimensional kernel, closed range and finite-dimensional cokernel with index dim ker − dim coker exactly as def-fredholm-operator-cokernel-and-index; lem-local-finite-dimensional-reduction-for-a-fredholm-map cites lem-fredholm-splitting-and-parametrix, which supplies precisely the closed splittings X = ker T ⊕ X_1, Y = ran T ⊕ Y_0 with bounded projections and dim Y_0 = dim coker T that the lemma assumes; prop-the-index-of-a-fredholm-map-is-locally-constant cites thm-fredholm-index-is-locally-constant, whose statement gives an operator-norm neighbourhood of Fredholm operators on which the index is constant, and the proposition's chartwise reading (continuity of p ↦ Df(p) in the chart coordinates) adds no hypothesis. No domain, quantifier, hypothesis or direction is changed.

Citations are used only for the stated propositions: def-compact-linear-operator for the definition of compactness, lem-finite-rank-operators-are-compact and lem-compositions-with-a-compact-operator-are-compact for compactness of finite-rank truncations and bounded composites, thm-norm-limit-of-compact-operators-is-compact for norm limits in the trace-class ideal and the square-root lemma, and thm-riesz-schauder-spectrum-of-a-compact-operator in ex-volterra-operator-is-hilbert-schmidt-and-quasinilpotent only for the facts that a nonzero spectral value of a compact operator on a complex Banach space is an eigenvalue of finite algebraic multiplicity and that 0 ∈ σ(K) when the space is infinite dimensional, exactly as stated there; the spectrum definition of def-spectrum-and-resolvent-of-a-bounded-operator is used verbatim.

The Hilbert–Schmidt convention used is exactly the cited one: relative to a supplied Hilbert basis E, with s_E(T) the finite-subset supremum of Σ_{e∈E}‖Te‖² and no choice in the definition. thm-hilbert-schmidt-operators-are-compact is used only for its clause 3 (an operator Hilbert–Schmidt relative to E is compact) and thm-hilbert-schmidt-norm-is-basis-independent only for ‖T*‖_{HS,F} = ‖T‖_{HS,E}; the AC_ω and supplied-basis hypotheses are preserved, and no existence of a Hilbert basis is inferred.

The only citing item is lem-compact-convolution-operators-decompose-into-finite-dimensional-invariant-subspaces; its [L2] states the spectral theorem's clauses faithfully (nonzero eigenvalues real, finite-dimensional eigenspaces, closed span of the eigenspaces equal to (ker T)^⊥ and to the closure of the range), and its step 2.1 applies it to the compact self-adjoint T_k, noting that AC supplies the AC_ω the theorem assumes.
